problem.text: Andre solved an equation, but when he checked his answer he saw his solution was incorrect. He knows he made a mistake, but he can't find it. Where is Andre's mistake and what is the solution to the equation? \(-2(3x-5)=4(x+3)+8\); work shown: \(-6x+10=4x+12+8\); \(-6x+10=4x+20\); \(10=-2x+20\); \(-10=-2x\); \(5=x\)
problem.answerKey: Mistake in the third line: when adding 6x to both sides (or collecting terms), 10 = 10x + 20, so -10 = 10x and x = -1. Worked: -6x + 10 = 4x + 20, so -10 = 10x, x = -1. Check: LHS -2(3(-1) - 5) = -2(-8) = 16; RHS 4(-1 + 3) + 8 = 4(2) + 8 = 16.
problem.gradingNotes: Accept x = -1. The mistake can be described as an arithmetic or combining error in moving terms from line 2 to line 3.

rubric.description: 1 pt: identifies Andre's mistake in combining or moving terms from line 2 to line 3 (e.g. 10 = 10x + 20 instead of 10 = -2x + 20)
